effects: The signature lets anyone call cancelAuthorization, which sets _authorizationStates[authorizer][nonce] = true (EIP3009._cancelAuthorization).
A pending transferWithAuthorization or receiveWithAuthorization of the authorizer that uses this nonce can never be executed after that.
No USDT0 or native currency moves, and no allowance changes.
formats.shown: The screen says "Cancel USDT0 authorization" with the Authorizer address, and the nonce as a raw bytes32 that wallets may hide.

findings.title: CancelAuthorization hides the nonce by default, but the nonce is the only value that picks which authorization gets cancelled.
findings.fix: Set the `nonce` field to "visible": "always" and change its label to "Nonce of authorization to cancel". Keep it out of interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: CancelAuthorization: the nonce stands for a transfer whose amount and recipient the message does not carry.
findings.evidence: EIP3009.sol: `CANCEL_AUTHORIZATION_TYPEHASH = keccak256("CancelAuthorization(address authorizer,bytes32 nonce)")`. The amount and recipient are in the earlier TransferWithAuthorization message, not here.

findings.title: The CancelAuthorization intent does not say that it cancels a pending signed USDT0 transfer.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: "Cancel USDT0 authorization". The code only cancels EIP-3009 transfer and receive authorizations, which use the same nonce space (EIP3009.sol _markAuthorizationAsUsed / _cancelAuthorization). A signer can read 'authorization' as an ERC-20 approval and expect an allowance revoke.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Cancel a signed USDT0 transfer".
